analysis.overall: You spent 78% of the day in range with a strong average of 132 mg/dL, though higher-carb meals led to noticeable peaks above 200 mg/dL after breakfast, lunch, and late dinner.

events.title: Breakfast spike from Rice and Kadi
events.description: After eating 75g of carbs, glucose rose steadily over two hours to a peak of 204 mg/dL before small automated corrections brought it back down.

events.title: Lunch peak and afternoon drop
events.description: A 50g carb lunch drove glucose up to 209 mg/dL around 2:11 PM, but insulin activity brought levels back into range and down near 70 mg/dL by late afternoon.

events.title: Late evening rise
events.description: Carbs eaten across two late-evening snacks pushed glucose up to the day's peak of 214 mg/dL near midnight, taking a couple of hours to settle.

events.title: Early morning dip
events.description: Glucose gently drifted down to 68 mg/dL during sleep before temporary basal adjustments helped bring numbers back into a safe range.

analysis.watch_for_tomorrow: Giving your meal bolus a few extra minutes before higher-carb meals like rice may help blunt those peaks above 200 mg/dL.
